key_insight: Aurora wraps a unified diffusion-based video editor with a tool-using agent that converts casual user intents into model-ready inputs (prompts, references, spatial masks) and orchestrates edits, removing the need for users to supply precise references or grounding.
problem_solved: Bridges the gap between real user requests and unified video editing models that expect pre-crafted text, reference images, and spatial grounding for local edits—enabling natural-language, underspecified, or partially-specified edit requests to be executed reliably.
method: Agent-driven planning: an LLM-style agent interprets the user's intent, breaks it into edit steps, and decides which tools to call.

Tool orchestration: the agent invokes specialized tools (reference retrieval, object tracking/localization, mask generation, prompt refinement) to produce the inputs the unified diffusion transformer needs.
Iterative edit loop: the system applies edits with the diffusion editor, verifies temporal consistency and visual quality, and performs corrective tool calls until the result matches the intent.
impact: Makes advanced, unified video editing models accessible to non-expert users and production pipelines by automating prompt engineering, reference assembly, and spatial grounding—reducing setup overhead and enabling more flexible, composable editing workflows.
